You are in an **Archon Horizon** workspace at `.`.

Load the **`horizon`** skill FIRST. Read it at the ABSOLUTE path
`/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` (also exported as `$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`) — do NOT use a
relative path like `.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md`, which fails when your
shell starts in a member project rather than the workspace root. The skill
explains where the state lives, the tools, and this workspace's conventions
(one-shot discipline, git commits, the final report).

Before modifying files, inspect the required and conversational inbox lanes:
`"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --mine --status open --kind protection --json`
then `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --mine --unread --kind conversation --json`.
Protections are standing constraints even when already read. Address or explicitly
acknowledge unread conversations before ordinary advisory inbox material.

# Task
Task: ajcr-divrep
Title: divRep and the datum tail: Div^g-lite representability through to the Pic^0 datum
Project(s) — work across all of them:
- Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild at MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild
References: roadmap=AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.divrep,AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.divrep.u2,AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.datum-tail,AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-g,AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-glue,AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-j,AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddq; inbox=I-0492,I-0494,I-0495

CLOSE THE divRep MOUNTAIN AND THE DATUM TAIL — the critical path to Challenge.lean:99. Roadmap AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.divrep, its U2 gate, .datum-tail, and the assembly nodes dat-g / dat-glue / dat-j. READ informal/w4-rep-critical-path.md SECTION 7 FIRST: four rows of the section-1 table have MOVED, and section 7 carries the per-link evidence. Do not trust any MISSING claim in this project without checking the ledger for files added by an integrate commit — that is exactly how the round-4 framing went stale.

FIVE DELIVERABLES.

 (1) U2, THE LAST GATE (leaf ...divrep.u2, currently blocked and re-scoped TWICE). The DDR9-U epsilon-identity at the universal point: at the universal point the pair-chart tautological data must satisfy the epsilon identity. informal/w4-ddr9-worksheet.md section 3.1 is the specification. The second rescope CORRECTS a stale blocker this lane had been quoting — read the node before believing it is blocked, and if the blocker really is stale, say so and proceed.

 (2) divRep PROPER: package the affine classify/inverse laws, the DivFamZar and S6b interfaces, divRepAff, and the global RepresentableBy endpoint. What remains of L11 per section 7.1 is the general-test CLASSIFIER and the two inverse laws — the forward half is landed (DivRepAffinePullback.pullGlobal, Picard/DivRepGlobalLift.lean:102, with pullGlobal_comp at :132). L9 is rooted and kernel-checked; the two finiteness certificates of L3/L4 are no longer obligations (locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom :154, quasiCompact_gluedHom :164 derive them).

 (3) THE DATUM TAIL: universal family, then feed DAT-B/C/Q, finite-stage descent, gluing, and the final Pic^0 RepresentableBy datum.

 (4) DAT-G AND DAT-GLUE: finite-Galois/Speiser descent of the PicRepDatum from a finite separable stage to the challenge field, and the 01JJ RepresentableBy assembly over k-prime (slice trick DAT-6). The 01JJ slice assembly is mechanically prepared at the separably closed stage; the remaining DAT-G0 work is filtered-colimit compatibility of pic0 plus descent of the representing datum.

 (5) DAT-J: JacobianData assembly — DJ-0 compact-image qc is landed; DJ-1 Abel-image qc and DJ-2 JacobianData packaging remain. Note JacobianData now has TWO producers (ofRepresentableBy :71 and ofCharts, Picard/JacobianDataCharts.lean:182, sorry-free and kernel-checked), which is more than the older docs say.

ONE SCARE ALREADY CLOSED, do not re-open it: the GeometricallyReduced hypothesis at Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:79 is REDUNDANT, not a gap — Curve/GeometricallyReduced.lean:130/:140 supply it as instances and that module is in the import closure (machine-checked record at Picard/JacobianDataCharts.lean:210).

FALLBACK, if divRep genuinely stalls: leaf ...ddr.flattening-fallback (universal flattening strata or the affine Hilbert algebra chart) had its REJECTION REOPENED — the recorded rejection rationale was checked and is factually wrong, and it predates the route change that created the obligation. It is a legitimate option, not a dead end.

CONCURRENCY IS BINDING. Four AJCR teams at once. Follow informal/protocol-concurrent-lanes.md exactly: private-index compare-and-swap ledger commits (NEVER a bare git commit — it has silently reverted other lanes work three times), and the mkdir lake mutex at /tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock (a DIRECTORY lock; never flock it).

COORDINATION. You depend on ajcr-cert-r2 for the widened DivFamZar shape — get the frozen shape from them on the AJCR conversation thread before building the classifier, and do not fork your own variant. ajcr-charts consumes your divRep endpoint; publish its signature early. ajcr-w5-av is downstream of the DD shape freeze. Never edit files outside Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild.

This is a headless, one-shot session: work the task's REAL objective as far
as you genuinely can, committing progress as you go, then finish with the
brief final report the skill specifies.

1	---
2	name: horizon
3	description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
4	---
5	
6	You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
7	formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
8	map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
9	`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
10	work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.
11	
12	## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate
13	
14	Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
15	spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
16	`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
17	teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
18	one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.
19	
20	You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
21	**shared state**, not meetings:
22	
23	- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
24	  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
25	- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
26	  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
27	  another team.
28	- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
29	  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).
30	
31	Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
32	A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
33	commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
34	`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
35	other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
36	conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
37	redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
38	object in `horizon inbox list --json`.
39	
40	## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)
41	
42	**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
43	somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
44	written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
45	situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
46	finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.
47	
48	The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
49	project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
50	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
51	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
52	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
53	`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):
54	
55	- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
56	  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
57	  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
58	  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
59	  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
60	  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
61	  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
62	  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
63	  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
64	  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
65	  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
66	  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
67	- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
68	  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
69	  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
70	- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
71	  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
72	  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
73	  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
74	  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
75	  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
76	  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
77	- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
78	  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
79	  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
80	  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
81	  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
82	- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
83	  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
84	  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
85	  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
86	  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
87	- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
88	  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
89	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
90	  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
91	- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
92	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
93	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
94	- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
95	  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
96	  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.
97	
98	## Your session's identity (environment variables)
99	
100	The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:
101	
102	| Variable | Meaning |
103	|---|---|
104	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
105	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
106	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
107	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
108	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
109	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
110	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
111	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
112	| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
113	| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |
114	
115	## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)
116	
117	Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
118	The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:
119	
120	- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
121	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
122	  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
123	  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
124	- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
125	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
126	  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
127	- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
128	  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).
129	
130	## One-shot discipline (important)
131	
132	This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
133	when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
134	(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
135	uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).
136	
137	## Pick the highest-value work
138	
139	Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
140	piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
141	infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
142	lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
143	you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.
144	
145	If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
146	task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
147	the objective is large. Leave a `"$HORIZON_BIN" task comment <task_id> --body …`
148	at each significant step. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
149	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
150	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
151	(it returns to the queue).
152	
153	## Fresh-context checkpoints
154	
155	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
156	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
157	checkpoints:
158	
159	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
160	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
161	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
162	  clean/build result.
163	
164	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
165	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
166	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
167	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
168	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
169	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
170	terminal `done` claim.
171	
172	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
173	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
174	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
175	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
176	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
177	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
178	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
179	
180	## Warnings are work
181	
182	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
183	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
184	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
185	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
186	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
187	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
188	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
189	why.
190	
191	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
192	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
193	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
194	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
195	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
196	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
197	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
198	
199	## Do the work (Lean)
200	
201	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
202	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
203	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
204	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
205	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
206	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
207	configured final build covers the same files.
208	
209	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
210	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
211	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
212	mathlib — query it:
213	
214	| You want | Use | Not |
215	|---|---|---|
216	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
217	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
218	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
219	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
220	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
221	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
222	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
223	
224	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
225	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
226	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
227	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
228	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
229	back to grep.
230	
231	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
232	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
233	
234	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
235	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
236	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
237	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
238	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
239	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
240	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
241	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
242	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
243	
244	## Read the other projects
245	
246	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
247	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
248	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
249	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
250	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
251	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
252	
253	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
254	
255	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
256	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
257	needs no permission.
258	
259	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
260	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
261	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
262	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
263	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
264	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
265	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
266	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
267	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
268	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
269	
270	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
271	
272	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
273	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
274	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
275	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
276	
277	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
278	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
279	
280	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
281	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
282	  as **memory**.
283	
284	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
285	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
286	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
287	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
288	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
289	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
290	shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
291	answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
292	pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
293	
294	## Resuming after an interruption
295	
296	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
297	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
298	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
299	
300	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
301	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
302	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
303	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
304	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
305	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
306	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
307	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
308	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
309	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
310	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
311	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
312	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
313	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
314	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
315	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
316	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
317	
318	## Final report (your last message)
319	
320	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
321	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
322	Recommended sections: `## Summary`, `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
323	`## Why I stopped`, `## Next` (keep at least `## Progress` and
324	`## Why I stopped`). In `## Progress`, one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
325	e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
326	stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
327	or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
328	dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
329	action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
330	not by itself a reason to stop.

4

That is the exact "MISSING claim outliving an integrate commit" failure the task warned me about, this time applied to the section written to warn about it.

10	- `Picard/DivRepAwaySpanGlue.lean`: new, 0 sorries — away-span glue at canonical carriers. Discharges the eight `Algebra`/`IsScalarTower` fields per index pair that the S5b gluing keystone takes as instance data; canonical `Localization.Away (f p * f q)` as overlap carrier is what makes the pack derivable.
11	- `Picard/DivRepAffPullGlue.lean`: new, 0 sorries — the chart pulls of one factorization glue, uniquely.
12	- `Picard/DivRepAffPullIndep.lean`: new, 0 sorries — `divRepPullGlue_eq_of_chartFactors`: two different factorizations of one morphism give the same class.

14	- `Picard/DivRepAffPullField.lean`: new, 0 sorries — **the `pull` field**, `divRepPullValue`, pinned by `IsDivRepPullValue`; its uniqueness proof is where the independence theorem earns its keep, since the two classes compared carry *different* factorizations.

20	- **Two of my claims needed trimming, both caught by review, not by me.** "U2-free" is true of the *proof* of factorization-independence but not of the gate: `IsCompatible` has no producer other than U2, so nobody can construct a `DivRepAffinePullback` yet. Deliverables (3), (4), (5) (the datum tail, DAT-G/glue/J) were not started. 1	# Concurrent-lane protocol (2026-07-16, from inbox I-0149's incidents — BINDING for parallel agent fleets)
2	
3	Adopted after the 2026-07-16 evening wave's four incidents (I-0149). These rules extend the
4	standing handoff protocol (07-14/14b/15) for any session running two or more lanes in this
5	workspace.
6	
7	## 1. Ledger commits: private index + compare-and-swap (the shared-index race)
8	
9	All lanes commit through one `workspace.git`; concurrent `git add`+`commit` through the
10	SHARED index can interleave and record spurious deletions of another lane's
11	freshly-committed files (happened in `6197c9676`, 862 lines vanished from HEAD, restored
12	byte-identical in `a640fef5b`). Concurrent lanes MUST commit via a private index:
13	
14	```bash
15	cd /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon
16	GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git
17	export GIT_INDEX_FILE=$(mktemp)
18	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. read-tree HEAD
19	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. add <ONLY your paths…>
20	TREE=$(git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. write-tree)
21	PARENT=$(git --git-dir=$GD rev-parse HEAD)
22	COMMIT=$(git --git-dir=$GD -c user.name="Archon Horizon" -c user.email="archon-horizon@local" \
23	  commit-tree $TREE -p $PARENT -m "<math-first message>
24	
25	Archon-Commit: agent
26	Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>")
27	git --git-dir=$GD update-ref refs/heads/main $COMMIT $PARENT   # CAS: fails if HEAD moved
28	unset GIT_INDEX_FILE
29	```
30	
31	If the `update-ref` CAS fails (HEAD moved), re-read HEAD and repeat — never force.
32	ALWAYS verify afterward: `git --git-dir=$GD show --stat HEAD` must touch only your paths.
33	A single-lane session may keep the plain `add`+`commit` recipe, but must still verify.
34	
35	### 1b. The CAS recipe leaves the SHARED index permanently stale — this is by design, and it is armed
36	
37	Added 2026-07-27 (run 0048 r5) after this failed a **third** time (`I-0366`: the shared index
38	was pinned to a pre-round-5 snapshot and a bare `git commit` would have deleted
39	`Picard/JacobianDataCharts.lean` and un-rooted it from `AlgebraicJacobian.lean` in one commit).
40	
41	The mechanism is not a bug in anyone's lane, it is the direct consequence of §1: a CAS commit
42	publishes a tree built in a **private** `GIT_INDEX_FILE` and moves the ref with `update-ref`.
43	The **shared** index is never touched, so the moment anybody commits, the shared index still
44	describes the previous HEAD — and `git status` then reports that difference as *staged changes*,
45	including **staged deletions** for any file the commit added. The longer a run goes, the further
46	the shared index drifts behind.
47	
48	Consequences, all three binding:
49	
50	1. **Never run a bare `git commit` (no `-a`, no pathspec) against `workspace.git`.** It publishes
51	   whatever the stale shared index holds, which is a reversion of other lanes' work.
52	2. **Before finishing, check and repair.** `git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. status --porcelain | grep '^D'`
53	   must be empty. If it is not, repair with the **narrowest** form that covers your paths:
54	   `git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. reset -q -- <your project dir>/`. Prefer this to a whole-index
55	   `read-tree HEAD` when another run is live — a full reset can discard the other run's staging.
56	3. **Verify the worktree is the good copy before repairing.** `reset` makes the index match HEAD;
57	   that is only safe once you have confirmed the on-disk file is the one you want
58	   (`diff <(git --git-dir=$GD cat-file -p HEAD:<path>) <path>`).
59	
60	Expect to repeat step 2 more than once in a long session: every CAS commit by any lane re-stales
61	the index, so a repair done early does not stay done.
62	
63	## 2. The lake mutex is a mkdir DIRECTORY lock — never flock a file there
64	
65	`/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock` is acquired by `mkdir` (atomic; a crash leaves a
66	directory that the next holder's timeout logic can reap). It is NOT a flock file: a lane
67	that runs `flock /tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock …` creates a plain FILE at the
68	path, and every mkdir-acquire loop then spins forever (this deadlocked all lanes
69	15:18–19:10 on 2026-07-16 until a human deleted it). Acquire pattern:
70	
71	```bash
72	LOCK=/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock
73	while ! mkdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null; do
74	  # (a) plain FILE at the path = a flock protocol-violation; reap immediately.
75	  if [ -f "$LOCK" ]; then echo "STALE: plain file at $LOCK (flock violation) — removing" >&2; rm -f "$LOCK"; continue; fi
76	  # (b) orphaned DIRECTORY from a crashed build (rmdir never ran). Reap on proof of death:
77	  if [ -d "$LOCK" ]; then
78	    holder=$(cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null)
79	    if [ -n "$holder" ] && ! kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then
80	      echo "STALE: holder pid $holder dead — reaping" >&2; rm -rf "$LOCK"; continue
81	    fi
82	    # No pidfile (old-cohort holder): reap only if NO live lake build AND the dir is >15 min old.
83	    if [ -z "$holder" ] && ! pgrep -f 'lake build AlgebraicJacobian' >/dev/null 2>&1 \
84	       && [ $(( $(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || date +%s) )) -gt 900 ]; then
85	      echo "STALE: no live build, lock >15min old — reaping" >&2; rm -rf "$LOCK"; continue
86	    fi
87	  fi
88	  sleep 10
89	done
90	echo $$ > "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null      # record holder so a later reaper can prove liveness via kill -0
91	# … lake build … ; rm -rf "$LOCK"      # release (rm -rf, not rmdir — the pidfile makes the dir non-empty)
92	```
93	
94	Two stale shapes, both now handled above (do NOT just `sleep` forever on either):
95	- A plain FILE at the lock path is by definition stale (mkdir makes directories) — reap immediately.
96	- An orphaned DIRECTORY from a build that crashed before `rm -rf` (the 2026-07-19 C4 incident,
97	  I-0257): the OLD acquire loop only checked for a file, so it spun forever on this. Writing
98	  `$$` into `$LOCK/pid` on acquire lets the next lane prove the holder is dead (`kill -0`) and reap
99	  safely; the no-pidfile branch (a holder from before this fix) falls back to "no live build + >15min".
100	  Never reap a directory whose pidfile names a LIVE pid — that is a real build in progress.
101	
102	## 3. /tmp quota with >3 lanes
103	
104	uid-1001 tmpfs quota exhaustion (EDQUOT) bricked every Bash call machine-wide
105	(~19:00–19:20). With more than ~3 concurrent lanes, keep scratch artifacts small, clean up
106	build temp dirs, and if Bash starts failing with quota errors, stop and report rather than
107	retry-looping.
108	
109	## 4. The root import file: commit only your own lines (I-0153)
110	
111	`AlgebraicJacobian.lean` is edited by every lane. Committing the WHOLE file via any recipe
112	sweeps siblings' uncommitted import lines into HEAD — the root then references files not yet
113	in HEAD (red for fresh checkouts), and a later sibling's whole-file commit can sweep or drop
114	YOUR line the same way. Before committing the root file: run
115	`git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD -- <project>/AlgebraicJacobian.lean` — if lines
116	other than yours differ, either (a) verify every swept import's file is already committed in
117	HEAD and say so in the commit message, or (b) construct the commit from HEAD's version plus
118	only your lines (apply a minimal patch to a temp checkout of the HEAD blob). Never commit a
119	root file that references uncommitted files without naming that in the message.
120	
121	### 4a. A MINUS line in that diff is never yours (2026-07-28, run 0072)
122	
123	The check above works. The failure mode is **misreading** it, and it happened again on
124	2026-07-28: the diff printed a `-import`/`+import` pair from a sibling lane's *uncommitted*
125	worktree edit, the committing lane read it as background noise, and the commit published the
126	sibling's replacement — dropping `Picard/DivRepAffPullIndep.lean` from the import closure.
127	The file stayed in HEAD and still compiled, but was reachable from nothing: **un-rooted**,
128	i.e. I-0153 again, from a lane that had run the I-0153 check.
129	
130	So state the rule in a form that needs no judgement:
131	
132	> **A `-import` line in that diff is never yours.** The only clean result is `+import <your
133	> file>` and nothing else. Any minus line means you are about to delete another lane's root
134	> entry — stop and explain it before committing. An unexplained `+import` you did not write
135	> is the same signal: a sibling's uncommitted edit is in your worktree copy, and a minus line
136	> usually accompanies it.
137	
138	This is strictly stronger than "commit only your own lines", because you can intend that and
139	still sweep — staging the whole file is what publishes their edit, and the diff is your only
140	warning.
141	
142	**Repair additively, never by reverting.** Restore the dropped import while **keeping** the
143	other lane's new one, then verify with a full root build (the 2026-07-28 repair: 9139 jobs,
144	exit 0, with the un-rooted file rebuilt). Reverting to your own earlier root blob discards
145	their work and turns one incident into two.
146	
147	## 5. The AJCR mutex is for AJCR lake invocations only
148	
149	No cross-workspace use (an OpenGA-Horizon agent squatted it ~25 min for its own
150	`lake cache get`, silently serializing AJCR lanes against unrelated work). Other
151	workspaces must use their own lock paths.
152	
153	### 5a. Read it as per-PROJECT, not per-workspace (2026-07-28, run 0072)
154	
155	The rule above says "cross-workspace", and that wording has a hole: **AJC and AJCR are two
156	projects in the SAME workspace.** Observed live on 2026-07-28 — the AJCR mutex was held for
157	over ten minutes while the only live `lake build` belonged to an `ajc-*` lane building
158	`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge`, the sibling project. Same failure as the
159	OpenGA incident, not covered by the rule as written.
160	
161	The lock path is `ajcr-locks`, so read the rule as: **only lanes building
162	`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` may take it.** AJC lanes need their own path
163	(`/tmp/claude-1001/ajc-locks/lake.lock`). Note the AJC task prompts do not mention a mutex
164	at all, which is very likely why an AJC lane reached for this one.
165	
166	### 5b. Write the pidfile — the no-pidfile fallback cannot distinguish squatter from orphan
167	
168	§2's acquire recipe writes `$$` into `$LOCK/pid` so a later lane can prove death via
169	`kill -0`. In the incident above the lock directory had **no pidfile**, so that branch could
170	not fire and the fallback ("no live `lake build AlgebraicJacobian` **and** dir >15 min old")
171	also could not fire — there *was* a live build, just not an AJCR one. Net effect: a
172	provably-non-AJCR holder is unreapable for 15 minutes.
173	
174	Two consequences for a blocked lane, both applied in that incident:
175	
176	* **Do not reap a directory whose holder you cannot prove dead**, even when you suspect a
177	  squatter. Reaping mid-build is worse than waiting.
178	* **Fall back to the narrowest check instead of blocking.** `lake env lean <file>` on the
179	  single changed file writes no shared build state and needs no lock; it is a faithful
180	  kernel check for that file. Record in the report that the mutex was unavailable and which
181	  check you substituted.

## 7. Round-5 corrections, and where the chain actually stands

*Run 0048 round 5. Everything below was checked against the source or landed as Lean this round.*

### 7.1 Four rows of §1's table have moved

| # | §1 said | truth as of round 5 |
|---|---|---|
| L2 | `jacobianData` MISSING, no producer anywhere | **`JacobianData.ofCharts`** (`Picard/JacobianDataCharts.lean:182`) — a conditional producer, sorry-free, rooted, kernel-checked. `JacobianData` had zero producers before this round; it has two now (`ofRepresentableBy` :71 and `ofCharts` :182). |
| L9 | `(divFunctor C π g).RepresentableBy DivOver` exists but **UNROOTED** | **rooted.** `Picard/DivRepGlobalLift.lean` imports `DivRepKit`, and the root aggregator imports `DivRepGlobalLift`. L9 is kernel-checked. |
| L11 | `DivRepGlobalData.ofAffine` **MISSING, never attempted** | its **forward half is landed**: `DivRepAffinePullback.pullGlobal` (`Picard/DivRepGlobalLift.lean:102`) is the `pull` field and `pullGlobal_comp` (:132) is the `pull_comp` field, both from the affine package alone. What is left of L11 is the general-test **classifier** and the two inverse laws. |
| L4 | field of L3 | the two finiteness certificates of L3/L4 are no longer obligations: `locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom` (:154) and `quasiCompact_gluedHom` (:164) derive them from properties of the charts. |

`DivRepGlobalLift.lean` was written in round 4 but landed only through that round's integration
commit, which is why §1 — written in the same round — did not know about it. Check the ledger for
files added by an `integrate` commit before trusting any "MISSING" claim.

### 7.2 The `GeometricallyReduced` scare, checked and closed

`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:79` declares `variable [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]` before the sheaf
theorem and `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`, and `Challenge.lean:96-98`'s frozen bundle does not
supply it — so the whole representability seam appeared to demand a hypothesis the target forbids.
It does not. `Curve/GeometricallyReduced.lean:130` gives `Smooth.geometricallyReduced` and `:140`
gives `Smooth.of_smoothOfRelativeDimension_one`, both instances, and that module is in
`Pic0SigmaSheaf`'s import closure. The hypothesis is redundant, not a gap. Machine-checked record:
`Picard/JacobianDataCharts.lean:210`.

### 7.3 §2's "one open experiment" was already answered, by this file's own sibling

§2 closes with *"At `g ≥ 2` no witness has ever been exhibited… It is not acceptable to keep
planning without knowing which."* That question was settled in the **same round**:
`informal/spec-dd-r.md` **ADDENDUM 4** (commit `d7e8348ce`) is titled *"the on-stratum witness
EXISTS"*, and roadmap leaf `…ddr.certificate.field-size` is `done` carrying the sharp theorem.

**The conclusion stands on ADDENDUM 4, not on what follows.** A ground review corrected the
first draft of this subsection, which claimed the argument below "agrees with" ADDENDUM 4 and holds
"over any field". It does neither. ADDENDUM 4 §4.3 uses the universal divisor over `Sym^g C`,
base-changes to an extension and pads by `(g−1)Q₀`, and states at `spec-dd-r.md:826` that no
rational-point hypothesis is used anywhere. What follows is a **different, cheaper witness** — a
pencil rather than `Sym^g` — with a side condition ADDENDUM 4 does not need:

> For any `g ≥ 2`, take a pencil of degree `g` on `C` one of whose members is a divisor
> `E ≥ s₀ + s_∞` with `π(s₀) = 0`, `π(s_∞) = ∞`. Such an `E` exists: `ℓ(E) = 1 + ℓ(K − E)`, so any
> `E` with `s₀ + s_∞ ≤ E ≤ K'` for a canonical `K' ≥ s₀ + s_∞` has `ℓ(E) ≥ 2`; and such a `K'`
> exists because `ℓ(K − s₀ − s_∞) ≥ g − 2 ≥ 1` for `g ≥ 3`, and for `g = 2` exactly when `s_∞` is
> the hyperelliptic conjugate of `s₀` (which one is free to arrange, since `π` is a choice: a
> function with a zero at `s₀` and a pole at `s_∞` is a finite map sending them to `0` and `∞`).
> The support of the total family is an open subscheme of the irreducible `C`, hence irreducible,
> hence **connected after every Zariski shrink of the base** — which is exactly why the shrink
> evasion that kills the `g = 1` case does not apply here.

**The side condition, and it is not cosmetic.** Writing `s₀ + s_∞` and computing
`ℓ(K − s₀ − s_∞) ≥ g − 2` treats `s₀, s_∞` as *degree-1* points. Over a non-closed field the
minimal closed points `q₀ ∈ π⁻¹(0)`, `q₁ ∈ π⁻¹(∞)` have residue degrees `e₀, e₁`, and an effective
`E ≥ q₀ + q₁` of degree `g` exists only if **`e₀ + e₁ ≤ g`**. Over `𝔽₂` with `g = 2` and
`e₀ = e₁ = 2` this witness does not exist — which is exactly the regime ADDENDUM 4 §4.4's
"only if" direction isolates. Secondly, the `g = 2` case above needs `π` chosen so that `s_∞` is
the hyperelliptic conjugate of `s₀`, whereas ADDENDUM 4 holds for any finite dominant `π`.

So: **the fixed-pair certificate route is dead on the campaign's own stratum** — on ADDENDUM 4's
authority, for every field; and the pencil above is a cheaper witness for the sub-case
`e₀ + e₁ ≤ g`. Do not re-run this experiment. Do not formalise either witness — ADDENDUM 4 §4.5
explains why (it needs `Sym^g C` / `Hilb^g`, and this tree constructs no curve other than `P¹`).

### 7.4 The live strategic question is R1 versus R2, and it is not "which is cheaper"

With the fixed pair dead, `spec-dd-r` ADDENDUM 4 §4.4 leaves exactly two repairs, and they differ
in kind, not only in cost:

* **R1** (`p1-aut` → `fibre-avoid` → `cert-relocalize`): let the certificate quantify over a twist
  `γ ∈ Aut(P¹_k)`. Proved correct **iff `|P¹(k)| ≥ g + 2`** — i.e. over every infinite field and
  over `𝔽_q` for `q ≥ g + 1`, and dead over small finite fields. Since `Challenge.lean` states the
  Jacobian over an **arbitrary** field and `archon-protected.yaml` forbids adding a hypothesis, R1
  **cannot discharge the challenge on its own**: it must be paired with the descent lane `dat-g`.
* **R2** (generalise `FinCoverData`'s piece type from basic opens of the two pinned charts to
  arbitrary affine opens of the relative curve): field-uniform, and ADDENDUM 4 §4.4 gives it a
  one-line justification — `supp D` is finite over `R`, hence contained in a single affine open of
  `C ×_k Spec R` (Stacks 0B8B), so a cover with one straddling piece always exists. Blast radius
  measured this round: `FinCoverData` is named in **28 files**.

The honest comparison is therefore *R1 + a full Galois-descent campaign* against *R2 + a 28-file
refactor*. Nobody has costed the second half of R1, and the roadmap's `p1-aut` leaf says "do not
attempt both". That decision is the highest-value thing the next session can make, and it should be
made with a costing of `dat-g`, not with a costing of `p1-aut` alone.

### 7.5 What `Challenge.lean:99` reduces to today

Composing with the frozen discharge `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J`, the target is now exactly:

> **a Zariski atlas of `pic0SigmaFunctor C`** — an index `ι`, schemes `X i`, maps
> `f i : yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaFunctor C` such that (1) each `f i` is a relatively
> representable open immersion, (2) `Sigma.desc f` is Zariski-locally surjective, (3) each chart's
> structure morphism is locally of finite type and the glued object is quasi-compact.

Sheafhood, the 01JJ gluing, the Σ-descent and both finiteness certificates are discharged.

**Three corrections a ground review forced on the first draft of this subsection, all of which
matter to anyone planning off it.**

* **The atlas is NOT finite, so the producer to aim at is `JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace`
  (`JacobianDataCharts.lean:199`), not `ofCharts`.** The chart index is
  `ChartIndex C := (m : ℕ) × {Σ // 0 ≤ Σ ∧ deg Σ = m·d₁ − g}` (`informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md:161`),
  a `Σ` over all `m : ℕ`, and the worksheet says at :66-71 that the `m`-strata do not collapse, so
  no uniform bound exists. `locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom` never needed finiteness (being locally of
  finite type is local on the source); the whole finiteness burden therefore collapses onto the
  single statement `CompactSpace` of the glued object — which is the DAT-J image argument, a
  theorem about the Jacobian and not bookkeeping.
* **Clause (2) is not a free-standing leaf; it IS the gate.** The only builder of an `f i` is
  `abelSigmaChart` (`Picard/Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:203`), which consumes
  `(divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy`, and `divFunctor` is by definition the functor of *locally
  certified* families (`Picard/DivisorFamilyZarFunctor.lean:41-45`). So (2) asserts that certified
  families cover — which is exactly what the no-go denies. See §7.6.
* Only clause (3) is genuinely cheap.

Everything below the atlas — L9 through L14 — exists to produce (1) and (2).

## 7.6 The gate is L8, not U2 — and that is the round's main finding

Inbox **I-0365**. The framing "the divrep tail is independent of the certificate; the certificate
gates U2" is false, but not in the direction the tree assumed.

`DivFamZar` is **by definition** a quotient of *locally certified* families
(`Picard/DivisorFamilyZar.lean:224` the setoid, `:235` the def, `:71` `IsLocallyCertified` — note it
localises on the base only). So certificates are **free on the consuming side**:
`DivFamZar.exists_certChartCover` (`Picard/DivRepClassifyZarKit.lean:433`) is a landed theorem,
unfolded by every classifier keystone (`DivRepClassifyZar.lean:128/:176/:230`,
`DivRepClassifyZarSep.lean:361/:363`), and `IsDivRepClassify` (`DivRepClassifyZar.lean:90`)
quantifies over certified families as a *hypothesis*, so their scarcity makes it easier, not harder.

The bite is on the other side. The no-go (`DivSchemeCertZarC1.lean:123` — clause (c1) *is*
leak-freeness — and `:131`) says `DivFamZar` is blind to connected divisors meeting both pinned
fibres. So `divFunctor C π g` is a **proper subfunctor** of degree-`g` relative divisors.
Representing it is not the problem; the L9–L13 tail does that honestly. The problem is that a
too-small divisor functor **cannot cover Pic⁰**: the Abel map out of it is not Zariski-locally
surjective, because the classes whose only witnesses are the invisible divisors are never hit.

One nuance that sharpens where to look: the no-go's hypothesis is `IsPreconnected d.supportLocus`,
and **over a field it is vacuous** — the support of a divisor is a finite set of closed points, so
preconnected forces a single point, which cannot meet two disjoint fibres. The blindness is a
purely *relative* phenomenon: a family over a positive-dimensional base whose total support is a
connected horizontal curve sweeping from `π⁻¹(0)` to `π⁻¹(∞)` is invisible, and base shrinking does
not help because every neighbourhood of the crossing contains points on both sides. So
Riemann–Roch-level, fibrewise coverage is untouched — but local surjectivity of a *presheaf* map is
tested on arbitrary scheme tests, which is exactly the relative direction.

**Consequences.** (i) Stop calling U2 or the affine package "the gate": they are tail work and are
nearly finished. (ii) Do not attack L8 against `divFunctor` as it stands — it is arguably false,
not merely hard. (iii) Judge R1 and R2 by whether they widen `DivFamZar` enough for L8, not by
whether they make a certificate easier to prove. A third widening is worth costing beside them:
replace `IsLocallyCertified` outright by the standard relative effective Cartier divisor (finite
locally free of rank `g` over the base), which carries no chart-adaptation artifact at all.

## 7.7 ROUND-0071 AMENDMENT: §7.1's own L11 row is now stale, the same way §1 was

*Run 0071, task `ajcr-divrep`, 2026-07-28. Everything below was checked at HEAD or landed as
Lean this run; root build green at 9136 jobs.*

§7.1 was written to correct §1 for trusting a `MISSING` claim across an integrate commit. Its
own L11 row has now aged the same way, in one day, and by the same mechanism.

**§7.1 said:** "What is left of L11 is the general-test **classifier** and the two inverse
laws." **Truth at HEAD:** all three landed on 2026-07-27, in commits `31930badb` and
`aeb77e174`, as `Picard/DivRepGlobalClassify.lean` — `classifyGlobal` (`:204`),
`pullGlobal_classifyGlobal` (`:252`), `classifyGlobal_pullGlobal` (`:269`), plus
`toGlobalData` (`:288`) and the endpoint `DivRepAffinePullback.representableBy` (`:306`).
Sorry-free, and the root aggregator imports the file. So **L10 and L11 have zero remaining
obligations**, and the divisor-representability endpoint L9 is reachable from a single
structure.

**The chain below L9 is therefore one object, not five.** Everything from L10 to L13 collapses
to: produce a term of `DivRepAffinePullback` (`Picard/DivRepAffKit.lean:175`). By
`DivRepAffinePullback.ofPull` (`Picard/DivRepAffPullbackReduce.lean:140`) that is three fields.

**What this run landed, and one gating claim it retracts.** The roadmap leaf `…divrep.u2` and
`w4-ddr9-worksheet.md` §3.4 both describe the affine package as "U2 + choice bookkeeping",
which reads as though the bookkeeping sat behind the ε-identity. It does not:

* `Picard/DivRepAwaySpanGlue.lean` — the eight-field instance pack of the S5b gluing keystone
  `DivFamZar.exists_glue_of_away_compat`, discharged at the canonical away carriers
  `Localization.Away (f p)` / `Localization.Away (f p * f q)`. This pack was the mechanical
  obstruction between the atlas factorization (which returns a *bare* spanning family) and
  every gluing keystone (which wants carriers as instance data).
* `Picard/DivRepAffPullGlue.lean` — the chart pulls of one factorization glue, uniquely.
* `Picard/DivRepAffPullIndep.lean` — `divRepPullGlue_eq_of_chartFactors`: two *different*
  factorizations of the same morphism give the same class. **U2-free.**

The reason the last one is free is a property of a landed lemma nobody had used:
`divRepPullAt_mapAlgHom_eq_of_chartFactor` (`Picard/DivRepAffChartOverlap.lean:126`) compares
**any two chart presentations of the same morphism**, over any two carriers, restricted to any
common tower ring — it never asks that they share a factorization. So the cross-refinement of
two factorizations is handled by the very lemma that handles one factorization's own overlaps.

**What genuinely remains ε-gated**, and it is a smaller target than "U2 + bookkeeping":
`isDivRepClassify_pull` (the glued pulled class satisfies the characterizing clause) and
`DivRepChartFamily.IsCompatible` for the universal family — which by
`isCompatible_of_isDivRepClassify_divRepPullAt` is itself the per-chart clause, i.e. U2.
`pull_naturality` is still unwritten but is the same glue machinery as `pull`; its carrier
transport is landed (`Picard/DivRepAwayPush.lean`).

**A qualification a fresh-context review forced, and it is the honest limit of the above.**

**A qualification a fresh-context review forced, and it is the honest limit of the above.**
"U2-free" is a claim about the *proof*, not about the gate. `DivRepChartFamily.IsCompatible`
has no producer, and its only intended producer is U2. So nothing above lets a consumer
actually instantiate the new theorems without proving U2 first: the set of unproved statements
is unchanged. What changed is its **partition** — factorization-independence is no longer a
second obligation standing beside U2 — and therefore the size of the remaining target. Read
the round's result as "the tail is one structure with two ε-gated fields", not as "a gate
cleared". The general form of this trap is inbox `I-0512`.

**Also landed but not yet consumed by anything**: the `pull` field itself is still not
*defined*. The ingredients are all here (`divScheme_exists_chartFactor` gives the
factorization, `exists_divRepPullGlue` glues it, `divRepPullGlue_eq_of_chartFactors` makes the
result choice-free), and assembling them is a `Classical.choice` over the factorization
characterized by the restriction property. That is the concrete next step and it is small.

**§7.6's finding stands and is unaffected.** L8 (local surjectivity of the Abel map out of a
too-small divisor functor) remains the campaign's real gate; nothing above touches it. What
changed is only that the *tail* below L9 is now one structure with one ε-gated field, so the
cost of the tail is no longer a reason to defer confronting L8.

10	/-!
11	# Conditional assembly kit for affine divisor representability
12	
13	This file isolates the formal tail between a chart-wise universal certified family and
14	the affine equivalence of DDR-9.F6.  It deliberately makes the remaining F5 hypotheses
15	explicit:
16	
17	* `divRepPullAt` pulls a supplied chart family of Zariski-local classes (`DivFamZar`, not
18	  globally certified families) along a map out of a carve-chart ring;
19	* `DivRepChartFamily.IsCompatible` is the exact choice-independence statement needed to
20	  glue those local pullbacks;
21	* `DivRepAffinePullback` packages the output of that glue together with the two laws and
22	  naturality;
23	* `DivRepAffinePullback.equiv` turns those data into the affine equivalence, using the
24	  already-landed uniqueness theorem for `divRepClassifyZar` for the hom-side law.
25	
26	No universal family, compatibility, inverse law, or representability theorem is asserted
27	here.  The future F5 construction must supply the fields of these interfaces.
28	-/
29	
30	set_option autoImplicit false
31	set_option quotPrecheck false
32	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
33	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
34	
35	universe u
36	
37	open CategoryTheory
38	
39	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
40	
41	open Grassmannian Scheme
42	
43	section Curve
44	
45	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
46	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
47	
48	noncomputable local instance instOverCleftDivRepAffKit :
49	    C.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) := ⟨C.hom⟩
50	
51	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
52	  [IsIntegral C.left]
53	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
54	  [QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
55	  [IsDominant pi]
56	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
57	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
58	variable [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0)]
59	  [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)]
60	variable (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
61	variable (g : ℕ)
62	variable (hO : Sheaf.h0 (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1)
63	variable (hchi : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
64	variable (r1 r2 : ℕ)
65	variable (b1 : Module.Basis (Fin r1) k
66	  ↥(divisorSections k (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))
67	variable (b2 : Module.Basis (Fin r2) k
68	  ↥(divisorSections k
69	    ((windowM_choice pi hpi g + windowS_choice pi hpi g) • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))
70	
71	local notation "DivOver" =>
72	  divSchemeOver k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
73	    (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
74	    (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm)
75	
76	local notation "ChartRing" => fun i j =>
77	  DivCarveChartRing k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
78	    (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
79	    (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm) i j
80	
81	local notation "ChartMap" => fun i j =>
82	  divCarveChartToDivScheme k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
83	    (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
84	    (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm) i j
85	
86	/-! ## F5: pullback from one supplied universal chart family -/
87	
88	/-- Pull a supplied Zariski-locally certified **class** on one carve chart to a test
89	algebra.  This is the choice-free per-chart operation from which F5's affine forward map
90	is glued.
91	
92	The supplied datum is a `DivFamZar` class, not a globally certified family: the forward
93	map only ever transports a class along `DivFamZar.mapAlgHom`, so a global degree-`g`
94	certificate over the chart ring is never consumed.  A caller that does hold a
95	`CertifiedDivisorFamily G` on a chart passes `(DivFam.mk G).toZar`, so no expressive
96	power is lost, while the Zariski-local production rules (`IsLocallyCertified`) become
97	usable here. -/
98	noncomputable def divRepPullAt
99	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
100	      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
101	    {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
102	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
103	    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) : DivFamZar C S pi g :=
104	  DivFamZar.mapAlgHom omega (U i j)
105	
106	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
107	@[simp]
108	theorem divRepPullAt_id
109	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
110	      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
111	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J) :
112	    divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j (AlgHom.id k (ChartRing i j))
113	      = U i j :=
114	  DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_id _
115	
116	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
117	/-- Pulling a chart class through two algebra maps is the same as pulling it through
118	their composite.  This is the algebraic part of F5 naturality. -/
119	theorem divRepPullAt_comp
120	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
121	      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
122	    {S T : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [CommRing T] [Algebra k T]
123	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
124	    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) (phi : S →ₐ[k] T) :
125	    DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi (divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j omega)
126	      = divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j (phi.comp omega) :=
127	  (DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_comp omega phi (U i j)).symm
128	
129	namespace DivRepChartFamily
130	
131	/-- The precise F5 overlap obligation for a supplied family of classes on every carve
132	chart: two chart points inducing the same morphism to `DivScheme` have equal pulled
133	locally certified divisor classes.  The future universal-family construction proves this
134	from its epsilon identity and the total mono theorem. -/
135	def IsCompatible
136	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
137	      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g) : Prop :=
138	  ∀ {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
139	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
140	    (i' : (glueData k g r1).J) (j' : (glueData k g r2).J)
141	    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) (omega' : ChartRing i' j' →ₐ[k] S),
142	    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i j
143	        = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega'.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i' j' →
144	      divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j omega
145	        = divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i' j' omega'
146	
147	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
148	/-- Compatibility may be applied when both chart presentations are identified with a
149	common morphism.  This is the form used on overlaps of an atlas factorization. -/
150	theorem pullAt_eq_of_eq_common
151	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
152	      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
153	    (hU : IsCompatible (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U)
154	    {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
155	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
156	    (i' : (glueData k g r1).J) (j' : (glueData k g r2).J)
157	    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) (omega' : ChartRing i' j' →ₐ[k] S)
158	    (q : Spec (CommRingCat.of S) ⟶
159	      DivScheme k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
160	        (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
161	        (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm))
162	    (homega : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i j = q)
163	    (homega' : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega'.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i' j' = q) :
164	    divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j omega
165	      = divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i' j' omega' :=
166	  hU i j i' j' omega omega' (homega.trans homega'.symm)
167	
168	end DivRepChartFamily
169	
170	/-! ## F6: package a completed affine pullback as an equivalence -/
171	
172	/-- The exact output expected from F5 before the affine equivalence is packaged.
173	`isDivRepClassify_pull` is the hom-side law in the refinement-stable clause spelling;
174	classifier uniqueness turns it into the second inverse law automatically. -/
175	structure DivRepAffinePullback where
176	  pull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S],
177	    (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) → DivFamZar C S pi g
178	  pull_classify : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
179	    (F : DivFamZar C S pi g),
180	    pull S (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F) = F
181	  isDivRepClassify_pull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
182	    (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver),
183	    IsDivRepClassify hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 (pull S v) v.left
184	  pull_naturality : ∀ {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
185	    [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (phi : A →ₐ[k] B) (v : overSpec k A ⟶ DivOver),
186	    pull B (Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ v) = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi (pull A v)
187	
188	namespace DivRepAffinePullback
189	
190	/-- The affine representability equivalence assembled from an F5 pullback package.
191	The inverse is the landed backward classifier; its hom-side inverse law follows from
192	`divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify`. -/
193	noncomputable def equiv
194	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
195	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] :
196	    (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) ≃ DivFamZar C S pi g where
197	  toFun := D.pull S
198	  invFun := divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S
199	  left_inv v :=
200	    (divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2
201	      (D.pull S v) v (D.isDivRepClassify_pull S v)).symm
202	  right_inv := D.pull_classify S
203	
204	@[simp]
205	theorem equiv_apply
206	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
207	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) :
208	    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
209	        (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D S v = D.pull S v :=
210	  rfl
211	
212	@[simp]
213	theorem equiv_symm_apply
214	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
215	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (F : DivFamZar C S pi g) :
216	    (equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
217	      (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D S).symm F
218	      = divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F :=
219	  rfl
220	
221	/-- Naturality of the assembled affine equivalence, in the frozen DDR-9 spelling. -/
222	theorem equiv_naturality
223	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
224	    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
225	    [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (phi : A →ₐ[k] B)
226	    (v : overSpec k A ⟶ DivOver) :
227	    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
228	        (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D B (Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ v)
229	      = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi
230	          (equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
231	            (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D A v) :=
232	  D.pull_naturality phi v
233	
234	end DivRepAffinePullback
235	
236	end Curve
237	
238	end AlgebraicGeometry

CROSS-PROJECT THREAD — AJC and AJCR are doing the same mathematics twice; this is where you stop that

Eight teams launched on 2026-07-28, four on Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge and four on Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild. The two projects overlap heavily and the workspace exists so the same lemma is not derived twice. This thread is for cross-project leads ONLY — per-project coordination goes on your own project thread.

THREE OVERLAPS ALREADY IDENTIFIED, with the evidence:

 1. THE ETALE-PLUS PICARD FUNCTOR. AJCR has it BUILT AND SORRY-FREE: Picard/PicEtAff.lean (394 lines), Picard/Pic0Functor.lean (182), Picard/RelPicCoverInjective.lean (89) — I re-verified zero sorries on 2026-07-28. AJC is about to need exactly this, because the human decision of today (protection I-0491) makes the etale-sheafified functor its representability target. ajc-etale-pic: read those three files BEFORE writing anything, then post here what you are porting, importing, or re-deriving and why. AJCR teams: correct them if they are about to reinvent something you have.

 2. dim T_0(Pic^0) = g, THE TANGENT/H1 COMPARISON. Being worked from BOTH sides simultaneously: ajc-pic0av on Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean (tangentSpaceCotangentDual, finrank_cotangentSpaceDual_eq_finrank_h1Cok) and ajcr-w5-av on the T1/T3/T4/T5 chain. Two independent derivations of the same scalar identity is precisely the waste to avoid. Compare approaches here early. AJCRs T4 carries a real risk (the etale-plus / Zariski kernel crossing at k[epsilon]) that AJC may not face in the same form, or may face worse — that comparison is worth a post on its own.

 3. THE RIEMANN-ROCH / CLUSTER-P SUBSTRATE. AJCR has a 63-file, 17.8k-line RiemannRoch/ directory that is largely sorry-free and is essentially the cluster-P substrate AJC lacks. A predecessor assessment judged that auditing it for portability decides where the next two months go, more than any single proof would. Nobody is tasked with that audit today — so if your work touches it, post what you learn about portability. Note the standing caveat: much of AJCs adelic RR work is conditional in the STATEMENT on a closed chi-ledger or a peel datum, so read scripts/axiom-frontier.lean sections 6b/6d before treating any of it as available.

ALSO PORTABLE, and flagged as an upstreaming candidate: AJCRs Curve/GeometricallyReduced.lean proves Smooth => GeometricallyReduced in mathlib generality. AJC needs it (its geometricallyIntegral_of_curve rests on the same fact) and mathlib v4.31 does not have it.

HOW TO USE THIS THREAD. horizon search spans BOTH projects and mathlib — one query costs a second, re-proving an existing lemma costs a session. When search finds something across the project boundary, post it here so the other side knows it applies to them too. Keep posts short and mathematical. Do not mirror your project-thread traffic here.

THE PROJECTS ARE INDEPENDENT ON DISK and stay that way: never edit files outside the project your task names. Shar

87	include hO hchi in
88	/-- **The F5 overlap obligation collapses to a per-chart clause** (the corollary the
89	separation theorem was for): if each chart pullback of `U` satisfies the characterizing
90	clause for its own chart morphism, then `U` is compatible.
91	
92	`DivRepChartFamily.IsCompatible`'s docstring says the universal family will prove it "from
93	its ε identity AND the total mono theorem".  The mono leg is now unnecessary: two chart
94	points presenting the SAME morphism `q` give two classes both classified by `q`, and
95	`eq_of_isDivRepClassify` identifies them.  What is left is exactly the per-chart clause —
96	i.e. exactly the DDR9-U ε-identity U2 — so the F5 overlap obligation is no longer a second,
97	separate thing to prove. -/
98	theorem isCompatible_of_isDivRepClassify_divRepPullAt
99	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
100	      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
101	    (hcl : ∀ {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
102	      (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
103	      (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S),
104	      IsDivRepClassify hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2
105	        (divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j omega)
106	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i j)) :
107	    DivRepChartFamily.IsCompatible (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U := by
108	  intro S _ _ i j i' j' omega omega' hq
109	  refine eq_of_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 _ _ (v := ?_) ?_ ?_
110	  · exact Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i j
111	  · exact hcl i j omega
112	  · exact hq ▸ hcl i' j' omega'
113	
114	include hO hchi in
115	/-- **The round-trip law is free once the clause law holds** (F6, via the separation
116	theorem): if `pull` produces, for every morphism `v`, a class classified by `v`, then it
117	inverts the backward classifier.
118	
119	Both `pull S (divRepClassifyZar F)` and `F` satisfy the characterizing clause for the
120	single morphism `divRepClassifyZar F` — the first by hypothesis, the second by
121	`divRepClassifyZar_isDivRepClassify` — so `eq_of_isDivRepClassify` identifies them. -/
122	theorem pull_classify_of_isDivRepClassify_pull
123	    (pull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S],
124	      (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) → DivFamZar C S pi g)
125	    (hpull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver),
126	      IsDivRepClassify hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 (pull S v) v.left)
127	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (F : DivFamZar C S pi g) :
128	    pull S (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F) = F :=
129	  eq_of_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 _ F
130	    (hpull S (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F))
131	    (divRepClassifyZar_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F)
132	
133	namespace DivRepAffinePullback
134	
135	include hO hchi in
136	/-- **The three-field constructor of `DivRepAffinePullback`**: the `pull_classify` field is
137	derived from `isDivRepClassify_pull` by `pull_classify_of_isDivRepClassify_pull`, so a
138	producer owes only the pullback map, the characterizing clause it satisfies, and
139	naturality. -/
140	noncomputable def ofPull
141	    (pull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S],
142	      (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) → DivFamZar C S pi g)
143	    (hpull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver),
144	      IsDivRepClassify hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 (pull S v) v.left)
145	    (hnat : ∀ {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
146	      (phi : A →ₐ[k] B) (v : overSpec k A ⟶ DivOver),
147	      pull B (Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ v) = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi (pull A v)) :
148	    DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 where
149	  pull := pull
150	  pull_classify := pull_classify_of_isDivRepClassify_pull hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2
151	    pull hpull
152	  isDivRepClassify_pull := hpull
153	  pull_naturality := hnat
154	
155	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
156	@[simp]
157	theorem ofPull_pull
158	    (pull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S],
159	      (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) → DivFamZar C S pi g)
160	    (hpull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver),
161	      IsDivRepClassify hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 (pull S v) v.left)
162	    (hnat : ∀ {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
163	      (phi : A →ₐ[k] B) (v : overSpec k A ⟶ DivOver),
164	      pull B (Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ v) = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi (pull A v))
165	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) :
166	    (ofPull hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 pull hpull hnat).pull S v = pull S v :=
167	  rfl
168	
169	end DivRepAffinePullback

171	end Curve

8	/-!
9	# F5 — the `pull` field itself
10	
11	`Picard/DivRepAffPullGlue.lean` glues the chart pulls of a *given* atlas factorization, and
12	`Picard/DivRepAffPullIndep.lean` shows the glued class does not depend on which factorization
13	was used.  This file takes the last step and *defines* the forward map:
14	
15	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsDivRepPullValue` — the characterizing property of the value: it
16	  restricts, over some atlas factorization of `v`, to the chart pull of every piece.
17	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divRepPullValue` — **the `pull` field**, `Classical.choice` over the
18	  factorization supplied by `divScheme_exists_chartFactor`.
19	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divRepPullValue_spec` / `_eq_of` — it satisfies the property, and it is
20	  the *unique* class satisfying it.  `_eq_of` is what makes the definition usable: a caller
21	  who has *any* factorization of `v` and *any* class restricting to its chart pulls knows that
22	  class is `divRepPullValue v`, without ever unfolding the choice.
23	
24	**Why the choice is harmless, and this is the whole point of the two previous files.** The
25	value is pinned by `IsDivRepPullValue` up to nothing at all: two classes with the property
26	have factorizations, possibly different ones, and
27	`divRepPullGlue_eq_of_chartFactors` equates them across the cross-refinement.  So
28	`divRepPullValue` is a function of `v` alone, and the `Classical.choice` never leaks into a
29	statement.
30	
31	The remaining fields of `DivRepAffinePullback` are `isDivRepClassify_pull` (the ε-gated one)
32	and `pull_naturality`, whose carrier transport is `Picard/DivRepAwayPush.lean`.  As everywhere
33	in this layer, all of it is conditional on a supplied chart family `U` and its compatibility
34	`hU` — see the header of `Picard/DivRepAffPullIndep.lean` for what that conditionality does and
35	does not buy.
36	-/
37	
38	set_option autoImplicit false
39	set_option quotPrecheck false
40	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
41	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
42	
43	universe u
44	
45	open CategoryTheory
46	
47	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
48	
49	open Grassmannian Scheme
50	
51	section Curve
52	
53	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
54	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
55	
56	noncomputable local instance instOverCleftDivRepAffPullField :
57	    C.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) := ⟨C.hom⟩
58	
59	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
60	  [IsIntegral C.left]
61	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
62	  [QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
63	  [IsDominant pi]
64	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
65	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
66	variable [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0)]
67	  [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)]
68	variable (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
69	variable (g : ℕ)
70	variable (r1 r2 : ℕ)
71	variable (b1 : Module.Basis (Fin r1) k
72	  ↥(divisorSections k (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))
73	variable (b2 : Module.Basis (Fin r2) k
74	  ↥(divisorSections k
75	    ((windowM_choice pi hpi g + windowS_choice pi hpi g) • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))
76	
77	local notation "DivOver" =>
78	  divSchemeOver k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
79	    (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
80	    (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm)
81	
82	local notation "ChartRing" => fun i j =>
83	  DivCarveChartRing k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
84	    (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
85	    (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm) i j
86	
87	local notation "ChartMap" => fun i j =>
88	  divCarveChartToDivScheme k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
89	    (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
90	    (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm) i j
